end.summary:
Practised observing and describing beaks, feet, claws, and leaf shapes.
Identified webbed feet as having skin between the toes and claws as pointed.
Linked beak and foot shapes to food and movement in 4/4 unaided attempts.
Named hooked, long pointed, and cone-shaped beaks with examples.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Atharv practised looking closely at bird features and linking them to eating or movement. They used the method of noticing shape first, then explaining its use, such as a pointed beak for catching fish and webbed feet for swimming. There was a mix-up between “walking in water” and “swimming” for webbed feet; swimming was stated later. At home, ask Atharv to observe one bird or plant and record two features and what each may help it do.
